# Writing an extension

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

An extension is a module that adds hooks, tools, commands and options to a session. These are the contract it implements and the handles its hooks are given.

Names: `Agents`, `Attachments`, `Basis`, `CURSOR_POINTS`, `Calibration`, `CalibrationError`, `CalibrationNewer`, `CalibrationStore`, `CallDraft`, `CommandHooks`, `Compaction`, `Count`, `CountJob`, `Counter`, `CounterAnswer`, `Cursor`, `CursorHook`, `CursorId`, `DefinitionError`, `Extension`, `Form`, `ImageRule`, `LabelName`, `Mcp`, `McpConfigError`, `McpServer`, `Model`, `NodeHandle`, `NodeId`, `Observation`, `Permissions`, `Prune`, `Reading`, `RequestCount`, `START_TIMEOUT`, `STOP_TIMEOUT`, `Skills`, `Span`, `SpanProof`, `StepLimit`, `Subject`, `TOOL_POINTS`, `TokenCalls`, `Tokenizers`, `Tokens`, `ToolHook`, `TreeHandle`, `UndoMarker`, `calibration_features`, `constants`, `counted`, `image_rule`, `reading`

## CalibrationStore

```python
class CalibrationStore
```

The calibration records under one directory (`$TAU_HOME/calibration`), one file per model.
Making one touches nothing: the directory is created by the first `observe`. A record's
`name` is a relative path ending in `.json` (`tau.Tokens` names them
`<provider>/<digest>.json`).

### CalibrationStore.__new__

```python
def __new__(cls, directory: str | PathLike[str]) -> CalibrationStore
```

### CalibrationStore.read

```python
def read(self, name: str) -> Calibration | None
```

The record named `name`, or `None` if there is none. `CalibrationNewer` for a record a
newer tau wrote, `CalibrationError` for a file that is not a record this build reads or
a name that is not a record's.

### CalibrationStore.observe

```python
def observe(
    self,
    name: str,
    key: tuple[str, str | None, str],
    markers: Mapping[str, str],
    span: tuple[Sequence[float], int] | None,
    time: str,
) -> tuple[Calibration, list[tuple[str, str, str, str, float]]]
```

Fold one reply into the record named `name` and return the record and what the fold
found. The file is locked, read, folded into and replaced, so two processes that observe
one model lose nothing of each other's. `key` is `(provider, base_url, model)`, for a
record that does not exist yet; `markers` the reply's drift markers; `span` the reply's
newest proved span as `(features, cost)`, or `None`; `time` when, as text the record
keeps. Each event is `(kind, name, was, now, by)`: `("marker", name, was, now, 0.0)`, a
drift marker that changed, or `("jump", "", "", "", by)`, a jump in what the model's
tokens cost (`by` is the relative change); either resets the record. Raises as `read`
does, leaving the file as it was.

### CalibrationStore.remove

```python
def remove(self, name: str) -> bool
```

Remove the record named `name`, whatever it holds; whether there was one.

### CalibrationStore.names

```python
def names(self) -> list[str]
```

The names of the records in the store, sorted; none if the directory does not exist.

## CountJob

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CountJob
    walk: tuple[Node, ...]
    model: str
    resolved: ModelConfig
    tools: tuple[str, ...]
    base: Count
    base_nodes: int
    known: Mapping[int, Count]
    unreported: tuple[int, ...]

```

What a counter is asked: the walk to count, the model (its qualified name, and

## Counter

```python
class Counter(Protocol)
```

What an extension offers as its `counter` attribute (at most one extension may). Both
methods are synchronous and do no network IO: the driver runs them in a thread. Core keeps
every report: an answer for a node a report covers fails the count with a
`DefinitionError`.

### Counter.count

```python
def count(self, job: CountJob) -> CounterAnswer
```

Count the nodes of `job.unreported`.

### Counter.observe

```python
def observe(self, observation: Observation) -> None
```

Learn from one reply. The driver calls it after every reply that reports its usage,
before the reply's `post_reply` hooks; a failure is told to the clients and costs the
step nothing.

## CounterAnswer

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CounterAnswer
    nodes: Mapping[int, Count]
    why: str | None = None
    total: Count | None = None
```

A counter's answer: a count for some of the job's `unreported` nodes, and `why` the rest
stay as weak as they are (or `None`). `total`, when given, is the whole request counted at
once, as a server's count endpoint counts it (D26 section 8): it replaces the sum of the
parts as `RequestCount.total`, and must be `rendered` or `calibrated`.

## Cursor

```python
class Cursor(TreeHandle)
    id: int
```

What a cursor hook acts through: one cursor, bound to its extension.

The tree handle, plus the cursor's own `move`, `write`, and `set_auto`,
which core allows only while a cursor hook job is out for the cursor. Once
the hook coroutine returns (`retire`), they raise `NotInHook`; so does every
other write and `ask`. Reads still work. Core checks no more than that the
tree stays valid (no hook edit limits).

### Cursor.node

```python
def node(self, id: int | None = None) -> Node
```

The node `id`, or the node this cursor is on when `id` is `None`.

### Cursor.walk

```python
def walk(self) -> list[Node]
```

The nodes from the root to the node this cursor is on.

### Cursor.options

```python
def options(self) -> Any
```

This extension's options at the cursor's `at` (its `options` dataclass); raises
`ConfigError` if it has none or what is set does not fit.

### Cursor.options_of

```python
def options_of(self, extension: str) -> Any
```

Another extension's options at the cursor's `at`, as `options` reads its own;
`ConfigError` if it has none (it is not loaded, or declares no `options`).

### Cursor.models

```python
def models(self) -> tuple[str, ...]
```

The qualified names of the models the catalog defines, in file order: what
`set_model` accepts.

### Cursor.tools

```python
def tools(self) -> tuple[str, ...]
```

The names of the driver's tools, the extensions' included, in the order a sample is
offered them: the names a `pre_sample` hook may put in `Subject.tools`.

### Cursor.show

```python
def show(self, text: str | None) -> None
```

Show `text` on this cursor to every client, as this extension's one line
(`CursorView.shown`); a later call replaces it, and `None` shows nothing. It is not in the
log or the scratchpad: it is gone when the session is reloaded, and dropped when the
cursor closes. `TypeError` for anything else.

### Cursor.set_model

```python
def set_model(self, model: Model) -> int
```

Write a `Config` node under `at` that sets the branch's `model` (a qualified name)
and move onto it, as `write` does. `ConfigError` if it is not configured; nothing is
written then. Returns the new node's id.

### Cursor.set_options

```python
def set_options(self, **changes: object) -> int
```

Write a `Config` node under `at` that sets these options of this extension (JSON
values) and move onto it, as `write` does: each replaces the walk's earlier value.
`ConfigError` if the extension has no options, or those that result, folded with the
walk's, do not fit its options type (a `__post_init__` that raises refuses); nothing is
written then. Returns the new node's id.

### Cursor.save_options

```python
def save_options(self, **changes: object) -> None
```

Write these options of this extension (JSON values) into the user's config file,
`extensions.<name>` in `<TAU_HOME>/config.json`, and have the driver read it at once. The
file is every session's and every branch's; `set_options` is this branch's, a node. No node
is written and nothing moves. The project's config is never written. `ConfigError` if the
extension has no options, the options that result (the layers, with these) do not fit its
options type, or the driver was given no user config; nothing is written then.

The file is read, changed and written back with no `await` in between, so on the event
loop (a hook, a tool, an async command) saves cannot interleave. It is not safe against
another τ process saving at the same moment (the last write wins, losing the other's
change), nor from sync commands that save at once on worker threads.

### Cursor.saved_options

```python
def saved_options(self) -> Mapping[str, object]
```

What the user's config file itself sets of this extension's options, as JSON values
(`{}` if it sets none, or there is no file): the value `save_options` changes, not
`options()`, which folds the project's layer, the overrides and this branch's nodes in.
To add to a list option in the file, read it here, not there. `ConfigError` if the
extension has no options or the driver was given no user config.

### Cursor.move

```python
def move(self, to: int) -> None
```

Move to `to` at once; later hooks see the new `at`. Raises `NoSuchNode`.

### Cursor.write

```python
def write(
    self,
    body: Body,
    delivers: Sequence[int] = (),
    *,
    copied_from: int | None = None,
    derived_from: int | None = None,
) -> int
```

Append `body` under `at` and move onto it, as one record; the
`delivers` items are removed. Returns the new node's id. `copied_from` and
`derived_from` as for `TreeHandle.append`.

### Cursor.reverse

```python
async def reverse(self, marker: int) -> bool
```

Have the extension that wrote the undo marker `marker` (D33) reverse what it marks:
its `async def reverse(self, cursor, marker)` is called with this cursor's handle, bound
to that extension, and the `UndoMarker`. Returns whether one did: `False` when that
extension is not loaded or has no `reverse`. The cursor does not move; what `reverse`
raises is the caller's. `ValueError` if the node is not an undo marker or no extension
wrote it, `NoSuchNode` if there is no such node.

### Cursor.set_auto

```python
def set_auto(self, on: bool) -> None
```

Turn this cursor's auto-step on or off. Wakes nothing: the step is running.
Turning it on inside a step that is aborted leaves the cursor at rest.

### Cursor.ask

```python
async def ask(self, text: str, expect: object = str, *, to: str | None = None) -> Any
```

Ask the cursor's clients `text`, and wait for an answer of type `expect` (any hint
of the type language; `str` by default). Returns the checked, converted answer, or
`None` if declined. `to` names the client asked first (`None`: anyone; a client that is
not connected is the same). The hook's job stays out meanwhile, however long and whoever
is connected, so the cursor is busy; an abort or go-to declines it (and any asked later
in that step). A `CursorId` answer of `"new"` opens a cursor at the cursor's `at`.

## DefinitionError

```python
class DefinitionError(TypeError)
```

A tool, command, extension or question that cannot be built: a parameter with no
annotation or one outside the type language, a default that does not fit its hint, an
injected parameter the function cannot have, a name taken twice, or an object that breaks the
`Tool` or `Extension` contract. The message names the extension, function and parameter.

## Extension

```python
class Extension(Protocol)
```

Hooks are methods named for their hook point, found by name and all optional.

Cursor hooks (`CursorHook`): `pre_step`, `pre_input`, `pre_sample`,
`pre_reply`, `post_reply`, `post_result`, `post_step`. Tool hooks
(`ToolHook`): `pre_tool`, `pre_result`. `name` is non-empty and unique among a
driver's extensions; any attribute named `pre_*` or `post_*` that is not a hook point is
refused when the driver is built (`DefinitionError`), so a misspelt hook cannot
sit silent. That covers data too: a dataclass field `pre_prompt` is refused. Name such a
field for what it holds (`prompt_prefix`, `before_prompt`), never with those two prefixes.

Optional attributes besides the hooks: `tools`, `commands`, `options`, `yields_names`,
`rescan` (`Rescanning`), and the lifecycle (D32 section 4): `async def start(self, tree:
TreeHandle) -> None`, run once before the driver takes its first job (and when a reload adds
the extension), handed a tree handle that stays live until `stop` returns; and `async def
stop(self) -> None`, run at shutdown (and when a reload removes it), after the tasks it
`spawn`ed are cancelled. A `start` or `stop` that is not a coroutine function is refused when
the driver is built (`DefinitionError`). A `start` that raises or outlives its timeout
(`START_TIMEOUT`, or `extensions.NAME.start_timeout`) stops the driver's start with
`ExtensionLoadError`; a `stop` that does is reported and the next one runs. And the undo
hook (D33): `async def reverse(self, cursor: Cursor, marker: UndoMarker) -> None`, which
reverses what an undo marker the extension wrote marks (a file checkpoint), called only
through `Cursor.reverse`; one that is not a coroutine function is refused the same way.

### Extension.name

```python
property name: str
```

The extension's name: letters, digits, `_` and `-`, unique among a driver's
extensions.

## Form

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Form
    name: str
    description: str
    schema: Json
    extension: str | None = None
    yields: bool = False
```

What a client knows of something it fills in: a command (its `name`, typed as `/name`,
its `description` and the `schema` of its arguments, with the named types' `"format"` and
each default, and the `extension` that owns it) or an extension's options (the `name` of the
extension, and a `schema` whose defaults are the values now; `extension` is `None`, as it is
for `/config`). A command is called by its `qualified` name, `extension:name`, which on the
wire a client writes itself from the two fields. A command that `yields` gives its bare name
up to any other command that has it (`/model` stays the built-in's; the yielding one is only
`/skills:model`). Frozen, compared by value, and not hashable:
the schema is a dict.

### Form.qualified

```python
property qualified: str
```

`extension:name` for a command, which nothing can take the name of; `name` for a form
with no extension.

## ImageRule

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageRule
    provider: str
    cap: int | None = None
```

How a model's images are counted (D26 section 7.3): by the rule of its `provider` (the
model's `provider` setting, the adapter that sends the request, never a guess from the model's
name) and its `image_tokens` setting, `cap`. `bound` says whether `tokens` is an upper bound:
it is for `anthropic` and `gemini`, whose published resizes cap every model they serve, and
for any model with a `cap`. Anything else (`openai`, which speaks to OpenAI and to every
OpenAI-compatible server, and a provider tau does not know) gets an estimate from the published
formulas, which a server that tiles or caps differently can exceed. On `anthropic` the `cap`
caps the visual tokens (the tier's published limit, 1,568 on the standard tier), and the
image's `ANTHROPIC_IMAGE_OVERHEAD` is added after it.

### ImageRule.bound

```python
property bound: bool
```

Whether `tokens` is the most an image can cost.

### ImageRule.tokens

```python
def tokens(self, width: int, height: int) -> int
```

What one image of `width` by `height` pixels costs at most (or, where not `bound`, is
estimated to cost).

### NodeHandle.ask

```python

```

Ask the batch's cursor's clients `text`, and wait for an answer of type `expect`
(any hint of the type language; `str` by default). Returns the checked, converted
answer, or `None` if declined. `to` names the client asked first (`None`: anyone; a
client that is not connected is the same). The call stays out meanwhile, however long and
whoever is connected, so the cursor is busy; an abort or go-to declines it (and any asked
later in that step). A `CursorId` answer of `"new"` opens a cursor at the batch's node.

## Observation

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Observation
    kind: Literal['reply', 'count_call']
    model: str
    resolved: ModelConfig
    walk: tuple[int, ...]
    usage: Mapping[str, int]
    markers: Mapping[str, str]
    tools: str
    span: Span | None
    time: int
```

One reply that reported its usage, as the driver shows it to the counter once the reply
is in the tree (D26 section 4), or one count call (D26 section 8). `kind` is `reply`, or
`count_call`. `model` is the qualified name of the model that replied and `resolved` its
settings in the catalog now; `walk` the ids of the nodes from the root to the reply; `usage`
the reply's normalized `meta.usage`; `markers` its drift markers by name (the served `model`,
`system_fingerprint`, and llama.cpp's `build_info`, `template_sha256`, `model_size`,
`n_params` and `n_vocab`, each as text, those the reply has); `tools` the digest of the tool
set its request offered (`tools_hash`); `span` the proved span that ends at this reply, or
`None` if the reply proved none; `time` the reply's time in milliseconds. For a
`count_call`, `walk` is the walk counted, `usage` is `{"input": N}` (the server's count of
the request it makes with the tools `tools`, before it is sent), `markers` is empty, `span`
`None` and `time` the newest node's.

## Reading

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading
    input: int
    output: int
    cached: int | None
    written: int | None
    reasoning: int | None = None
    tool_prompt: int | None = None
    written_1h: int | None = None
```

One reply's normalized `meta.usage` (D15, D26 section 2): `input` counts every prompt
token, `cached` and `written` the part read from and written to the cache, `written_1h` the
part of `written` kept for an hour, `tool_prompt` the part of `input` a built-in tool's use
added, and `reasoning` the part of `output` that was thinking. Each but `input` and `output`
is `None` when the server did not report it.

### Reading.said

```python
property said: Count
```

What the reply's words cost without its thinking: `output` less `reasoning`, a
`reported` count. Where thinking is taken out the bound is `REASONING_BOUND`, since a
server's thinking count "may differ by a small number" (D26 section 3.2).

## RequestCount

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequestCount
    total: Count
    base: Count
    base_nodes: int
    nodes: Mapping[int, Count]
    why: str | None = None
```

What the walk to a node will cost as a request (`Cursor.count`).

`total` is the whole request. `base` counts the walk's first `base_nodes` nodes and the
request's overhead (tool definitions, hidden prompts, per-message overhead) as one; it is
`NONE` with `base_nodes` 0 while no reply on the walk has reported its usage. `nodes` has one
count for each node that is sent, by node id, except a node inside a **lump**: where two
requests prove that the nodes between them cost a known sum, the first node holds the sum and
the others have no count of their own, so a cut never lands inside one. `why` says why the
total is weaker than it could be, or is `None`.

## Span

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Span
    nodes: tuple[Node, ...]
    cost: int
    proof: SpanProof
```

A proved span (D26 section 3): `nodes` are the nodes added between two consecutive
requests on one walk, from the first request's reply up to the node before the second's
reply; `cost` is what they cost together, the second bill's `input` less the first's, which
is exact because the first request is proved to be a prefix of the second; `proof` says
how.

## SpanProof

```python
SpanProof = Literal['cache', 'slot', 'prefix']
```

How a span is proved: `cache` (the second request read exactly the first from the server's
cache), `slot` (llama.cpp's slot held at least the whole first request) or `prefix` (the
provider found the first request to be a byte prefix of the second when it sent it).

## StepLimit

```python
class StepLimit
    name = 'step_limit'
    options = Options
```

Turns a cursor's auto-step off after `limit` unattended steps in a row (D1).

The limit is the extension's option (`Options.limit`, 50 unless configured), read at
each hook, so `/config step_limit` changes it for a branch.

It guards the loops where the cursor does move every step, such as a model
that calls tools forever or a hook that writes "continue" after every reply.
A cursor that does not move is stopped by core, not by this limit.

The count is this object's own memory, per cursor, kept at hook points:

- `pre_input` sets it to 1: the step that takes an input is the first. There
  is no `post_input` hook; `pre_input` fires once per input item offered.
- `pre_step` adds one, when the cursor's auto-step is on. A step run with
  auto-step off (a frontend's `step`, a load) is attended and is not counted.
- `post_step` turns auto-step off when the count has reached `limit`, and
  starts the count over, so whoever resumes the cursor (`set_auto`) gets
  another `limit` steps. It also starts over whenever it sees auto-step off:
  a halt, an abort, or a go-to ended the run.

When core turns auto-step off because a step did not move the cursor, that
happens after `post_step`: the count stays as it was until the next input.

A hook that leaves an input pending offers it again every step, so
`pre_input` restarts the count every time: this limit does not bound that.
Its hooks halt nothing, so they keep the default order 0 (D28): at a tie, load
position puts it after the built-ins before it by key and before every user
extension, so a user `post_step` at 0 sees auto-step already off and can stop
cleanly. A hook that turns auto-step back on from `post_step` after it wins over
the limit; one that wants to stay bounded by it orders its `post_step` below 0.

### StepLimit.__init__

```python
def __init__(self) -> None
```

### StepLimit.pre_input

```python
async def pre_input(self, cursor: Cursor, subject: Subject) -> str | None
```

Start the cursor's count at 1: the step that takes an input is the first.

### StepLimit.pre_step

```python
async def pre_step(self, cursor: Cursor, subject: Subject) -> str | None
```

Count this step if auto-step is on. A bad `limit` option fails the step here.

### StepLimit.post_step

```python
async def post_step(self, cursor: Cursor, subject: Subject) -> str | None
```

Turn auto-step off once the count reaches `limit`, then start the count over.

## Subject

```python
@dataclass
class Subject
    draft: Draft | None = None
    node: Node | None = None
    ending: Ending | None = None
    tools: Sequence[str] | None = None
```

The mutable thing a cursor hook works on, by hook point.

`draft` for `pre_input`, `pre_sample`, `pre_reply` (a hook may replace it;
from `pre_sample` it is a reply that answers the sample). `node` for
`post_reply` and `post_result`. `ending` for `post_step`. `pre_step` has
none.

`tools` is for `pre_sample` alone: the names of the tools this one sample is offered, or
`None` (the start) for all of them. What the hooks leave in it is the offer; the next sample
starts at `None` again. A name that is not one of the driver's tools, or any `tools` set at
another point, fails the step as a hook that breaks its contract does.

## TOOL_POINTS

```python
TOOL_POINTS = ('pre_tool', 'pre_result')
```

The names of the tool hook points.

## TokenCalls

```python
class TokenCalls
    name = TOKEN_CALLS
    needs_counter = True
    order: ClassVar[Mapping[str, int]] = {'pre_sample': CALL_ORDER}
    options = CallOptions
```

The built-in extension `token_calls` (D26 section 8), off by default (`tau ext enable
token_calls`).

Before a sample (`pre_sample`, ahead of compaction's hard limit) it asks the model's
provider for a count call (`Cursor.count_call`): the server's own count of the request the
walk makes. The driver shows the answer to the counter (`Tokens`), which gives it as the
`rendered` total of the walk's request count, so the hard limit reads the server's number
instead of an estimate. Only some providers count (`OpenAIProvider` on llama.cpp:
`/apply-template` and `/tokenize`); elsewhere a call answers nothing. A failed call is told
to the clients and the sample goes on with the counter's own count. It needs a counter: the
driver refuses it without one.

Option `when`: `straddle` (the default) calls only when the count's interval straddles the
hard limit (`tokens <= hard < upper`), an estimate that cannot say whether the request fits;
`always` calls before every sample.

### TokenCalls.pre_sample

```python
async def pre_sample(self, cursor: Cursor, subject: Subject) -> None
```

Ask the server to count the request about to be sent, when `when` says to.

### TreeHandle.counter

```python
property counter: str | None
```

The key of the extension that offers the counter (D26), or `None`: then `count` is
the meter's alone.

### TreeHandle.count

```python
async def count(self, at: int | None = None) -> RequestCount
```

What the walk to node `at` will cost as a request: a `RequestCount`, its `total` and a
count for each node. Every count is a report, or a ceiling (the node's bytes) for what no
report covers, unless the `counter` extension counts it better. `at` defaults to the
cursor's node (a `Cursor`) or the batch's (a `NodeHandle`); a tree handle must give it
(`ValueError`). `DefinitionError` if the counter counts what a report covers.

### TreeHandle.count_call

```python
async def count_call(self, at: int | None = None) -> int | None
```

The server's own count of the request the walk to node `at` makes, with every tool
offered (D26 section 8): the model's provider asks its count endpoint (llama.cpp's
`/apply-template` and `/tokenize`), and the counter is shown the answer, which it may
give as the `rendered` total of the next `count` of the same walk. `None` when the
provider has no count endpoint for the model (a hosted API, or a request with an
image). `at` defaults as `count`'s does. `SampleError` if the server fails the call.

### TreeHandle.spans

```python
def spans(self, at: int | None = None) -> list[Span]
```

The proved spans of the walk to node `at`, oldest first (D26 section 3): each is the
nodes between two consecutive requests whose cost the two bills prove, with how. A span
nothing proves is not listed, and neither is one a copy inherits (its count is in
`count`). `at` defaults as `count`'s does.

Append a node under `parent` without moving any cursor. Returns its id.
`copied_from` names the node this one repeats verbatim, `derived_from` the node whose


Append a root (a detached tree) holding `config`, without moving any

```python

```

Open a cursor at `at`; it wakes. Returns its id.

### TreeHandle.add_item

```python

```

Add this extension's item to a cursor's scratchpad; the cursor wakes.

### TreeHandle.remove_item

```python

```

Remove any item; raises `NoSuchItem`. Wakes nothing.

### TreeHandle.send

```python
def send(self, to: int, text: str, images: Sequence[Image] = ()) -> int
```

Send `text` to cursor `to` as a `User` message authored by this extension, with
`images` after it (D31), and turn its auto-step on: `to` takes the text at its next step
(through its `pre_input` hooks) and answers. Needs no client. Returns the item. At most
`MAX_INPUT_IMAGES` images, each an `Image` with its bytes or one the session keeps (only
its `sha256` is read then). They are held to the model of `to`'s branch by the image rule
a client's `send` meets: `ValueError` saying why they cannot go, `MissingImage` for one
the session does not keep, and nothing is sent then. The rule runs again after
`pre_input`; an input that fails there halts its step with why, which `rest` returns as
`Ending.Halted`.

### TreeHandle.tell

```python
def tell(
    self,
    text: str,
    *,
    to: str | None = None,
    cursor: int | None = None,
    level: NoticeLevel = 'info',
) -> None
```

Send `text` as a `Notice` from this extension to client `to`, or to every connected
client by default, about `cursor` at `level` (`"info"`, `"warning"` or `"error"`, D32
section 2). `cursor` defaults to this handle's own: a `Cursor`'s, the batch's cursor of a
`NodeHandle`, none (the session) for a tree handle. Dropped if `to` is not connected: a
notice is for someone who is there. One to every client told by the extension's `start`
(which runs before any client connects) **stands**: each client that connects later gets
it after its snapshot, until the extension is stopped. `NoSuchCursor` if `cursor` is not
open, `ValueError` for another level.

### TreeHandle.spawn

```python
def spawn(self, coro: Coroutine[Any, Any, object]) -> 'asyncio.Task[None]'
```

Run `coro` as a task the driver owns for this extension, and return it. An exception
in it (not its cancelling) is reported: an `error` `Notice` from this extension to every
client, `"task failed: Type: msg"`, and its traceback on stderr. The extension goes on.
The task is the extension's, whichever of its handles spawned it, so a hook may start one
that outlives it; the driver cancels and awaits it when the extension is stopped, before
its `stop` runs (at shutdown, and when a reload stops it). Not one of the driver's
effects: a harness's quiet does not wait for it. On the event loop only (`RuntimeError`
off it), `ConnectionError` once the driver has stopped or failed; `coro` is closed when
it is refused.

### TreeHandle.reassemble

```python
def reassemble(self) -> None
```

This extension's `tools` or `commands` changed (an MCP server listed its tools): the
driver assembles the tools and commands again from every extension, used from the next
job it dispatches (a job out keeps the tools it was dispatched with; a call to a tool
that has gone is `Err("unknown tool: ...")`). Hooks, options and hook order are not
touched. Clients get `Commands` if the forms changed. `DefinitionError`, with nothing
changed, if the new set does not fit (two tools of one name).

### TreeHandle.rest

```python
async def rest(self, cursor: int) -> Ending | None
```

Wait until `cursor` is at rest with no effect out, and return how its last step
ended; `None` if that is not known (it has not stepped since the session was loaded).
After a `send` to a cursor that was at rest, this is the ending of the step the send
caused. If the cursor was mid-step, the input waits for that step to end and this may
return that earlier step's ending with the input still pending: to wait for the step a
send causes, `rest` first, then `send`, then `rest` again. A cursor held by an open
question or a gate does not rest, so this waits as long as the cursor is held. Async
only: a sync tool, which runs on a worker thread, cannot call it. `ValueError` for this
handle's own cursor: waiting for itself would never end. No cycle between two cursors
is detected; the user's abort is the way out: when this handle's own cursor is aborted
(or sent elsewhere) while the wait is out, the wait ends at once and returns
`Ending.Aborted()`, so a hook, which an abort never cancels, learns it was aborted. The
cursor waited on is left as it is.

### TreeHandle.abort

```python
def abort(self, cursor: int) -> None
```

Abort `cursor`'s step as a client's `abort` does: cancel its sample or calls, stop
its command, decline its open questions, and turn its auto-step off. Safe from a sync
tool's worker thread: it returns once the event loop has done it. `ValueError` for this
handle's own cursor: aborting it would cancel this very call.

### TreeHandle.close_cursor

```python
async def close_cursor(self, cursor: int) -> None
```

Close `cursor`: abort its step as `abort` does, wait for it to rest, drop its pending
items, and close it (D17). It leaves `cursors()` and the clients' views; its id, its last
node (in `closed()`) and its labels stay, which is what `reopen` restarts from. Anyone
waiting on it sees the abort. `CursorClosed` if it is already closed. Async only, like
`rest`. `ValueError` for this handle's own cursor: closing it would wait on itself.

### TreeHandle.reopen

```python
def reopen(self, cursor: int) -> int
```

Open a new cursor at the closed `cursor`'s last node and move each of its labels
onto it, as this extension. Returns the new id. `ValueError` if `cursor` is open,
`NoSuchCursor` if it was never opened.

### TreeHandle.set_label

```python
def set_label(self, label: str, cursor: int) -> None
```

Set `label` on `cursor`; a label set elsewhere moves.

### TreeHandle.remove_label

```python
def remove_label(self, label: str) -> None
```

Remove `label`; raises `NoSuchLabel`.

## UndoMarker

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UndoMarker
    label: str
    return_to: int
    reverses: str
    priority: str = 'move'
    extra: Mapping[str, object] = field(default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({}))
```

One undo marker (the module docstring): `label`, `return_to`, `reverses`, `priority`
(`MOVE` unless given) and `extra`, the owner's own keys. `ValueError` for an empty `label` or
`reverses`, a `return_to` that is not a node id, a `priority` other than lower-case letters,
digits, `_` and `-`, or an `extra` key that is one of the four.

### UndoMarker.body

```python
def body(self) -> Body
```

The marker as the `Custom` node body to write (`cursor.write(marker.body())`).

### UndoMarker.of

```python
@classmethod
def of(cls, body: Body) -> 'UndoMarker | None'
```

The marker `body` holds; `None` if it is not a `Custom` of kind `undo`. `ValueError`
naming the problem for one whose data is not a marker's (not a JSON object, a key
missing, a value of the wrong kind).

## calibration_features

```python
def calibration_features(body: Body) -> list[float]
```

The features of a node's body, as the fit counts it: for each role (system, user, assistant,
calls, results, thinking) its text's lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, other
ASCII, whitespace, bytes of non-ASCII characters and words, then how many nodes of each role
(1 for the body's own). 48 numbers; a span's features are the sum of its nodes'. A `Config`
or `Custom` body, which is never sent, is all zeros.

## constants

```python
def constants(
    extensions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]],
    name: str,
    known: Mapping[str, type],
) -> dict[str, object]
```

The administrator keys the config layers set for extension `name` (`extensions` is
`LoadedConfig.catalog.extensions`): `known` maps each key it has to its type (`bool`, `int`,
`str`). `ConfigError` for a key it has not, and for a value of another type (a `bool` is no
`int`).

## counted

```python
def counted(node: Node) -> bool
```

Whether `node`'s reply counts toward usage: one a provider sampled (`node.by` is
`Author.Provider()`: an extension's answer to a sample reported no usage because it was never
billed), that is not a copy (`node.copied_from is None`) and not rewritten from another
(`derived_from`: a pruned reply keeps the `meta` of the sample it came from). This is the one
place the rule lives.

## image_rule

```python
def image_rule(model: ModelConfig) -> ImageRule
```

The `ImageRule` of a model: its provider's, with its `image_tokens`.

## reading

```python
def reading(node: Node) -> Reading | None
```

The `usage` a reply reports, or `None` if its provider reported none. `ValueError` for a
`usage` that is not the normalized shape or has more cached and written than input, or for a
reply whose provider kept the server's report (`usage_raw`) but could not normalize it; the
callers (`_read`) turn that into "no usage, and why", so a past node never fails a step.
